what_it_does: Modern servers can have two tiers of RAM: a small, very fast pool and a larger, slower pool. Deciding which data to keep in the fast pool — and when to move data between pools — is called memory tiering. Bad decisions waste bandwidth by moving data that didn't need to move, or leave the fast pool half-empty. ArtMem uses reinforcement learning (RL), a type of machine learning where a software agent learns good decisions by trial and reward, to continuously watch how the workload is behaving and adapt its migration policy on the fly. Instead of rigid rules ('move a page if it's been touched more than N times'), the RL agent can decide to move fewer pages, move different pages, or skip migration entirely when the situation calls for it.
